en:
It's nice to be able to take a few minutes and kick your feet out, huh? 

When I first got here, I thought it would be a constant struggle to survive, that I'd have a short, miserable life, and never be able to relax again. 

Funny how things don't turn out the way you think they will. 

I mean, who could've guessed that this island would be such a shit-show, right? 

|Not that it makes all that much difference for me, really. 

I mean, Lukatt is as good as anywhere else. 

I kept company with worse people than this before getting shipped out, so it's just the same shit in a different pile."

Rosaline stares into the fire for a moment, her bright smile gradually fading from her face, as she chooses her next mouthful of words. 

|"I was trained to be an assassin, you know. Can you imagine anything so stupid? 

Well, when I was a little girl I didn't think it was stupid. 

I came from a big family, and a poor one, so the day I saw the dancers' troupe come to town, and I told my parents that I wanted to be one, I was shocked when they said yes. 

Of course, my parents must've known that the dancers were something darker, that they would take little girls away and change them. 

I'm pretty sure they even paid my parents, thinking about it now, but at the time I was just a little girl having her wish come true.

|And to be sure, they did teach me how to dance. 

It wasn't until I was thirteen that I learned we would sometimes have to kill people.

Lots of girls were horrified when they found out, but not me. 

There was something romantic, I think, about the idea of being beautiful and alluring and also ridding the world of dangerous, evil people. 

I took to my training eagerly, and I was good at it, for a while.

|Eventually though, I started asking questions they didn't like. 

You see, I wasn't going to be ridding the world of dangerous people per se - I was going to be killing whoever was on their list. 

I had no way of knowing if those people actually deserved to die or not. 

Even the people who gave me the orders didn't know why. 

We were just expected to... to do it.

|I wasn't going to have any of that. 

I ran away, and I've been running for years. 

They don't let you leave, you see, so if you stay in one place for too long, they find you. 

And of course, they eventually did find me, and they pulled some strings to ship me out here, probably to scare the other girls into obedience. 

I guess even they didn't know what sort of place this really is.

|Well, screw them. 

I'm freer as a convict than I ever was as a dancer anyway, so it feels like a trade up. 

And you, well, we've kicked some asses, but because we had to, or because we wanted to, not because someone told us to, and that difference is everything to me."

Rosaline stands up, her cheerful smile creeping back across her face as she turns to go.

"I guess I'm just trying to say thanks.

After this is all over, I think I'll be a dancer for real. It would feel good to do something that just made people smile and laugh and enjoy themselves, wouldn't it? Something gentle and carefree. Something with less blood. Not that I'm pussing out, of course. Still lots of bloodletting left in me yet.
I'm not afraid of being on my own, of course, but I'm still willing to help. Are you sure that's best?
How are you doing today? Everything alright?
There's no rush. Just take things one day at a time and we'll be okay.
Alright then. Maybe I'll see you around, hey? Try not to get yourself killed.
A perfect opportunity to test my work!
I'll document this as a test case.
Fascinating.
What could it hurt?
We miscalculated.
That was unforeseen.
Did anyone else feel that?
The veins here are swollen.
I'm not ready to die yet, do you hear me?
Dammit. I've work left to do!
It'll be an invaluable experience.
Don't spout such senseless drivel.
I'll be sure to observe closely, then.
Well, that would hardly be surprising.
Oh, drat, I wasn't looking.
Is that really the best you could do?

It's good to be in the company of actual human beings again. And orcs, of course, nothing against orcs. It feels like it's been ages since I've been able to have an actual conversation with someone. I've rather missed it.
Tired of me already?
Ah hello. Do you require my services?
I know it's how some of us ended up here in the first place, but let's not be making hasty decisions, hmm?
Ah, pity. I was hoping things were going to get interesting. Well, good luck and all that.
I told you already! I'm not their king and never was!
Haven't I lost enough already?
You'll strip away my last vestiges of dignity? To hell with it then, and to hell with you.
Go from being prisoner to being slave? You'll have to kill me first!
I have no resistance left. As long as I can rest, I care not what you do with me.
I was just trying to leave in the first place, bloody lunatic!
Well, it isn't as though I have anything to gather up, so let's be off. The sooner we quit this place, the better.

I'm not sure what brought you to this place, but I'm certain enough that it wasn't for the purpose of rescuing me. Whatever you came here to do, I won't stop you. Have a picnic, or better yet, a bonfire. I never want to see another pygmy again.
Perhaps if I'd been cleverer I might have turned this rabble into something constructive. Ah well. I don't really care.
Go with you? I must say I like the thought of being in the company of someone taller than waist-height for awhile. Why not?
It's probably better that I take some time to shake off this disturbing experience before I dive headlong into another.

Have you got a moment? 

I've been hearing sordid rumours flying around about me, and how I came to be here. I thought I'd take the opportunity to set the record straight with you before you ended up hearing who-knows-what from God-knows-who."

Shapiro sits down by the fireside and smooths his robe out across his lap before continuing, stroking his beard thoughtfully.

"I was a professor at the academy of sorcery in Crest, and part of that position is devoting a certain amount of time toward research, developing new ways to use magic. There are many procedures to follow, of course, and much paperwork to file. Too much, if you ask me. 

|Most of my peers worked on flashy applications, but I didn't care to follow their lead. I worked on subtler things, ways to affect people. Charms, enchantments, curses, and such things. 

It's a fascinating field, but I'll get carried away if I talk about it, so you'll have to forgive me if I skip the details for the time being. 

In any event, some of my students took a great interest in my private work, and I began collaborating with a number of them. Some of them even volunteered to be personally experimented upon. 

This was, of course, against the rules of the academy, but we were so steeped in our work that it barely registered. 

|We did that for a few months, and things were going well. I was on the verge of several useful new formulae, and the students were engaging and enthusiastic. 

Then one of them died. We have no idea why or how, but one day, she simply died. There's no way it could have been the magic, I'm sure of it, but the other students began to panic. 

One of them went to the administrative board and reported what we'd been doing. 

Once that started, a whole inquisition opened up. The students all spoke against me at the hearings, and I was thrown into prison, branded as a charlatan, and shipped out here. 

|I didn't kill that girl, do you understand? Our experiments on her were concluded months prior to her death, and even if it had been the magic, she volunteered... begged even, to be the subject of those experiments. 

She was an intelligent adult woman capable of making her own decisions, and she understood that there could be risks. All of the other students endured similar experimentation with no ill effects. We were not dabbling in deadly arcana.

Truthfully, I suspected foul play by one of the other students, but I had scant proof of anything, and I knew that bringing that up in the hearings would only serve to drive myself upon the stake further. 

|So there you have it. Believe me or don't, that is the tale of Shapiro the wicked Charlatan, straight from his own mouth. When you hear the rumours, as you surely will, I trust you'll do me the courtesy of at least remembering what I've said. 

You know, just speaking of this has me quite sharp to edit some of the formulae I can still remember. Let me take fire watch, if you will, since I'll be awake anyway. 

And thank you for listening. You're fairer to me than I am used to, and it does not go unnoticed.

You know, I haven't had proper laboratory equipment for a long time, but for some reason I feel more comfortable in my sorcery than I ever have before. Maybe it's something about working without all the etiquette and procedures that I find liberating, or perhaps there's a certain affluence to Lukatt's veins? It hardly matters, I suppose.
Well that's sudden. Are you sure?
Ah, good to see you again. Was there something you needed?
If there's something bothering you, we'll address it. No need to be rash.
How disappointing.
You know, since coming here, business has never been better. No tarifs, no taxes, no regulations, no scruples. I should've come to this island years ago.
Hey buddy. Wanna see something cool?
I'll be off to secure some goods soon. Don't miss your chance to stock up!
Give me... your weapons... I can... forge...
Forge... I remember...
Why? What was... I building?

I ought to make a decisive move, soon.
Grrh... no, that won't work...
Hrmm...
It feels like we've been playing for quite a while.
We will need supplies for the next outing, yes? I will carry the load, so you may remain strong for battle. Just tell me what you need.
Greetings, friend.
Of course. I will be ready.
Pack's heavy today, an' lucky for you! My good fortune is your good fortune, right? Buy some of this stuff so I don't have to carry it all back.
Hey! You wanna buy somethin'?
Right. Well I'll be outta here come morning, so if you decide you want anything else, catch me before then.
Successful test.
I could win this game blindfolded, but shifting these pieces around is taking it out of me.
Hmm...
I forgot whose turn it is...
I do hate resorting to violence.

You need to be
taught some manners!
Is that of any import?
What is that for?
That is unforgivable.
Unacceptable!

This place could 
do with a cleaning.
Don't stray too far.

Then, it is time for
the blood to flow!

Let us paint in
strokes of death!

You're better than
you let on,.

Oh don't be 
so modest.
What foolishness.

Well, at least
you're honest.

That's really your
own fault.
That was inevitable.
Well, it's not a good deal of privacy, but it's also not the worst I could do. I catch the others staring sometimes, you know. It's hard not to be flattered by all the attention.
But whatever would I do by myself out there?
A pleasure to see you, of course.
Does it please you to see me distressed?
Well, I know better than to linger where I am not wanted. Good day to you.
Would you put an end to this madness?
Base banditry, is it? I think not. I am not without pride.
A fairer deal I think I shall not find. Take it.
That is not how you go about such things. I refuse.
Well, I can hardly blaming you for craving such a thing, can I?
A gracious offer. I take my leave.
Splendid. This promises to be most satisfactory.
I cannot tell you how refreshing it is to meet someone who knows how to have a civil conversation, and I could certainly find worse company. Perhaps you'd consider... extending our engagement?
Hello, stranger. To what do I owe the pleasure?
Why yes, of course. Who wouldn't want me along. Do you have proper arrangements made?
Well, you'd best put your affairs in order first. Do come and find me later.

Who would have thought such fine company could be found on such a wretched rock? Ever since joining you, I've found myself... enthralled by your manner of leadership. I found it curious at first, but I am beginning to understand. 

Know that I intend to remain for as long as you will have me. 

Take this, a small token of my esteem, and think of me whenever your eyes come upon it. Know that your company I treasure.

I realize how difficult it must be to lead a group this large all alone, so I have been trying to do my part. Some of the company you keep could well do with a lesson in civility, and really, who better to give it to them?
That wouldn't do at all. I beg you to reconsider.
It is always a delight to see you.
That was cruel of you. I'll need a moment to dry my eyes.
I was so close! Curse you!
I don't care who you are or what you did, as long as you deal with me in honest coin. I'll give you a fairer shake than any trader in Crest ever did.
Even convicts need supplies.
This is just a stopover as I make some rounds to a few other places. Get what you need before I go.
I know my way around the outdoors, and the wilds of Lukatt are no different from the wilds anywhere else. Still, it is nice to sleep in a camp every once in a while.
Care for some spoils from the wilds?
I'll be heading out in the morning. Maybe my travels will bring me back here. Maybe not.
You aren't going to win.
This doesn't end well for you.
That seems important.
I wasn't fast enough.
Don't worry, we'll... we'll do something!
Hmm. Nothing.
Maybe.
We shouldn't be here!
I see.. so much death!
We'll be fine. Trust me.
Today isn't the day for that.
You're not helping.
Just focus!
You could have done better.
What a waste.
It's a shame that none of the books we'll find here will be anything resembling recent. Near as I can tell, the last piece of print I found was at least a hundred years old. Just a guess, of course.
Oh, that's rather surprising. Are you sure?
Good day to you.
I see. Well don't do anything rash, now.
Well perhaps I'll head back to the archive, then. Wish me luck.
You are remarkably strong!
Wouldn't that be tidy? No, I think not!
I am beaten, then. Take it and leave me in peace!
Aren't I prisoner enough already?
I've little choice, it seems. Perchance you will be interesting.
Very well, the archive is yours.
Yes, marvellous! I'm sure you have plenty of interesting tales to tell.

I've been in this archive for months. I could survive here indefinitely, I suppose, but I admit it's been growing somewhat tedious, and I'm not sure what I will do if my health fails or I become injured. Perhaps it's time for a change of pace.
That book is quite a shock, I must say. Did you find it in the locked room?
You know, I was just thinking the same thing! It would be grand to have someone to talk to.
Well that is a shame. I suppose I will stay here until I figure out what to do next.

Are you available for a moment? I'd like a word. "

Vankan sits down, smoothing his kilt over his lap. He strokes his beard idly while staring into the flickering firelight.

"I haven't told you this yet, because it tends to freak people out, but I see things. Flashes of things. Flashes of you. Hell, it's what got me sent out here to this island in the first place. 

When I first realized that the things I see are real, I thought it was my obligation to help people, try to warn them about the flashes I saw, save them from the pain of their misfortunes if I could. And I could, so I tried.

|At first I was a novelty. People would come and visit the orc with the third eye, listen to me prattle on as I sifted through pictures of maybes and mights. People thought I was an entertainer, so I even made some money. I wasn't going to say no.

Well, I guess a bunch of people started realizing that I was telling the truth, that my flashes were real, and they started getting scared of me. People weren't coming to me anymore, and all of a sudden I wasn't helping anyone. 

It was that, more than the money, you know. I mean, could you stand by and let something awful happen to a bystander if you had the power to stop it? Wouldn't that feel just awful?

So... I tried.

|I tried so hard, that I became THAT guy. I was the orc standing in town square, with the crazed look in his eye, screaming doom because I was constantly bombarded with these images of rotten things happening to everybody who walked past. 

They would ignore me, and the dreadful things would happen, and I would feel awful for not stopping it, and I would try harder. 

They arrested me a few times, just put me in a cell with the drunks, assuming that I was a raving lunatic. Maybe I was, maybe I am. It's so hard to tell sometimes. 

|I kept doing it though, and I was so numb to the things I was actually saying, that one day I said it to someone powerful. A magistrate, I think. I barely remember. 

I told him to rush home, or he would never see his wife and daughter again, that they would be snatched from him. He scoffed at me, but of course I was right. They were taken by kidnappers and held ransom. 

He got them back and caught the men responsible, and then he asked them if I was involved with them. They, of course, tried to pin the whole thing on me. They rounded me up and put me on trial for kidnapping.

|Thankfully, I had enough of a reputation that it was fairly easy to convince them that I was just insane, and not actually dangerous. That magistrate though, he wasn't satisfied. 

He convinced the court that I was too much of a threat to be allowed to stay, and talked them into giving me a one-way trip to Lukatt. 

Sorta like everyone else, right?

|I've since decided that it's best to keep my flashes to myself. The more I ignore them, the smaller they get. Maybe it's just me looking into a place I'm not meant to look, after all. 

As for my flashes of you, I had a flash that there wouldn't be any soup left if you don't go now, so I came out to fire watch a little early. Go on, or you'll miss it. 

And thanks for listening. You've been good to me and I wanted you to know it's appreciated.
I love what we've done with this place. It's positively bustling! Well, compared to what it was like before we got here, I mean.
Is this because of that incident with the soup? I apologized already, didn't I?
Looking for me? Well, here I am!
You don't have to go rubbing it in my face. I already said I was sorry.
You really mean it, don't you? Fine then, I'll go, and I'll be taking my books with me!
I knew this was going to be a trap. I just knew it.
Thanks again.
We'll just pick up our stuff and be on our way. Thank you.
No problem.
That is a very weird smell.
That's it, we're dead.
We aren't gonna make it!
